verdicts.reason: The code fact is accurate — `set` updates an existing entry in place at :58-63 and never moves it. Whether that matters depends on how often prices are rewritten without being read, which the repository does not show: the only writer is the cache-miss path in get-price.ts, which always reads immediately after writing. Cannot be settled from the code.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:58-63 — `this.map.get(key)!.value = value; return` leaves the insertion order unchanged
src/cache/lru.ts:44-46 — `get` re-inserts the key, so a read refreshes recency
src/pricing/get-price.ts:18-24 — the only call to `set` is followed by a `get` of the same key
test/cache/lru.test.ts:40-52 — no case covers a write-only key

verdicts.reason: `Number('0')` is 0 and passes the NaN check, and the eviction loop at :66 then empties the map on every write. The impact is a cache that never hits, with no error or log line, so a misconfiguration is invisible.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:12 — `Number(process.env.PRICE_CACHE_SIZE ?? 500)`
src/cache/lru.ts:57 — only `Number.isNaN` is checked
src/cache/lru.ts:66 — `while (this.map.size >= this.capacity)` is always true at capacity 0

verdicts.reason: `get` never compares `expiresAt` with the clock. The reviewer's "long after five minutes" is right in principle, but on the measured call pattern every miss writes a new key and triggers the eviction loop, so stale entries are cleared within one write. A maintainability issue more than a live one.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:41-49 — no `expiresAt` check in `get`
src/cache/lru.ts:64-70 — the only expiry check is inside `set`
src/pricing/get-price.ts:18-24 — every miss calls `set`
test/cache/lru.test.ts:60-71 — the expiry test advances the clock and then calls `set` before `get`

verdicts.reason: The eviction test does write four keys, not three: the `beforeEach` at :12 seeds one entry before every case. With the seeded key the cache exceeds capacity on the third write in the case, and the assertion tests real eviction.
evidence: test/cache/lru.test.ts:12 — `beforeEach(() => cache.set('seed', 0))`
test/cache/lru.test.ts:31-38 — three further writes to a cache of capacity 3

verdicts.reason: The cache is module-level, so every test file that imports get-price.ts shares it, and the order tests run in decides which prices are already cached. The two pricing tests that assert a call to the pricing service pass only because they run first.
evidence: src/pricing/get-price.ts:6 — `const cache = new LruCache(...)` at module scope
test/pricing/get-price.test.ts:20 — asserts the service was called once
test/pricing/discounts.test.ts:14 — requests the same SKU earlier in the default run order
vitest.config.ts:8 — `isolate: false`, so modules are shared between files

verdicts.reason: The suggested `Map` iteration-order concern does not apply: a JavaScript `Map` iterates in insertion order by specification, so `keys().next()` is reliably the oldest insertion. The finding assumed hash-ordered iteration.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:67 — `this.map.keys().next().value`
src/cache/lru.ts:4 — the store is a plain `Map`
